clue.text: American state briefly put out of countenance by fruit

explanation.surface: An American is left disconcerted by a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' shortens the state's name to its usual abbreviation, Cal.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a gourd, the hard-shelled fruit of a tropical tree or vine.

clue.text: Newspaper feature with a capital heading

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a regular article by one writer

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it: a thing with a capital at its head
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an architectural pillar topped by its carved capital

explanation.walkthrough: A capital is both a large letter and the head of a pillar, so the word fits both the newspaper and the building.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a regular newspaper article and also a pillar crowned by a capital.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: alive, as in the quick and the dead

explanation.surface: A vicar's quickly done chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' in the old sense means alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's benefice is called a living, and the adjective also means alive.

parts.note: a try is an attempt or test

explanation.surface: A trial of banning something in the Irish Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bantry is a town on Bantry Bay in County Cork.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition locates a place within Ireland, and Bantry is a Cork town there.

explanation.surface: Theft is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'increase' comes after the theft in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing up on someone means creeping close without their noticing.

clue.text: Is general officer commanding able to return drink?

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so each abbreviation and verb is read from the end

explanation.surface: A question of whether a senior army officer can bring back a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Both GOC and CAN are reversed in place, each piece read backwards where it stands, giving COG then NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a strong spirit served as a drink.

clue.text: Openings available if I score incorrectly

indicators.note: a score done incorrectly is wrong, so its letters come in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Chances will open up if a player misses or miscounts a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orifices are holes or vents, openings into a body or cavity.

clue.text: Ring Eton about explosion of gas

indicators.note: about suggests being turned around, so these letters are moved
an explosion blows things apart, scattering the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone phones the school about a gas blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless gas that makes up most of the atmosphere.

definitions.note: playful: the quality belonging to the love god, read as his name plus a noun ending
definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: the state of being the archer god of love

explanation.surface: The lustful appetite of the archer of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupid is the Roman love god armed with bow and arrows; the answer looks like his name turned into an abstract noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupidity means avarice, an eager desire for wealth or possessions.

clue.text: Object in tennis star using perfume

indicators.note: the object is placed in the champion's surname, which holds it

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A tennis champion who wears a particular scent.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Laver won two calendar Grand Slams; END sits inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender water is a traditional scent distilled from the fragrant flowers of the plant.

parts.note: a tip is a prediction, as of a winner
the head or top of something

explanation.surface: A prediction made by a chief that turns out superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal adjective meaning first-rate or of the very best quality.

clue.text: Ferocious beast for chap to exercise

parts.note: to drill troops is to exercise them

explanation.surface: A wild animal kept for a man to train with.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large, powerful West African baboon with fearsome canine teeth.

indicators.note: going back means the short word for a lie is written from its last letter

parts.note: a fib is a small lie

explanation.surface: Someone lying low alongside an elderly lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifold means twofold, having two parts or layers, which is what double describes.

clue.text: Londoner carrying on business for profit

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: a resident of the capital
second meaning: a person investing for gain

explanation.surface: A Londoner running a money-making enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is jokey: someone who lives in the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalist invests money in trade for gain; split playfully, the word means a dweller of the capital.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pledge, especially to marry
second meaning: a booking for paid work, as for a performer

explanation.surface: Someone is offered the prospect of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a formal pledge to marry and a period of hired work for a musician or actor.

clue.text: Fool writing about worker soundly corresponding

parts.note: writing on a subject is writing about it

explanation.surface: An idiot writes a piece about a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' here means in sound, not thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonant words resemble each other in vowel sound, matching in how they are heard.

parts.note: surface reading: a broker, as a sort of dealer
setter's reading: the word before broker in the City dealer's title, plus an ending for a trader

explanation.definitionFit: A stockist is a shopkeeper or dealer who keeps a particular line of goods for sale.

indicators.note: turning into something different signals the letters are rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Power that has been turned into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'into' does double work in the surface but all its letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to have command or power over others.

parts.note: a set-to is a brief scrap
a written composition, as the score of a piece

explanation.surface: Points won in a dispute about a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' looks like winning points; it is a composer writing a score for words.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a text is to write a musical setting for it, putting the words to a tune.

clue.text: Looking out of sorts in uniform

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a servant's or guild's distinctive dress

explanation.surface: Someone appears unwell while dressed in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is an adjective from liver: irritable or queasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the special dress of servants or a company, and as an adjective means bilious or irritable.

clue.text: Turned up before artist in snappy outfit

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive

explanation.surface: Someone arrived ahead of a painter, dressed smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snappy outfit' suggests smart clothes; it is kit that takes snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is apparatus for taking snapshots, so it is jokingly an outfit for snapping.

clue.text: Food plant hired out to the Italian

explanation.surface: A crop let out to an Italian man.
explanation.definitionFit: The lentil is a leguminous plant grown for its edible seeds.

explanation.surface: A mistake that no Catholic tried to cover up.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is usually a blunder; here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, so in crossword terms it is a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Small girl has one appointment to confirm

parts.note: a short form of the name Valerie

explanation.surface: A little girl has a single meeting booked and wants it confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate something is to ratify or prove it sound, as confirming does.

indicators.note: something discovered within the city name is found among its letters, though not in their printed order

parts.note: the Philippine capital, taken as written

explanation.surface: Some beast has been found in the Philippine capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is not hidden in Manila letter for letter; the same six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature, a beast as opposed to a plant.

parts.note: a life is a written biography

explanation.surface: Someone takes only a modest interest in the income from a biography.
explanation.walkthrough: Liferent is a Scots law term.
explanation.definitionFit: A liferent is a right to use property or draw its income for one's lifetime only, an interest limited in time.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who sums, adding figures up

explanation.surface: Something wobbles dangerously during the warm season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but someone who sums; to tot up is to add, so a totter is one who adds.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to wobble on the point of collapse, and the noun also names a person who tots figures.

explanation.surface: Someone balks at causing problems for their backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jib' looks like a verb meaning to balk; it is the sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a triangular sail set on a stay, and a jib is one such foresail.
